name: ID-02
label: Likely R

key_factors: R+13 district with long-tenured incumbent Mike Simpson seeking re-election
Simpson holds an overwhelming fundraising edge ($1.3M raised vs. $161K for Gilbreath)
No public polling; Polymarket prices Simpson near 95%
Minor-party and Libertarian candidates on the ballot could siphon a few points
model.rationale: Simpson combines a thirteen-point Republican district lean, decades of incumbency, and an eight-to-one money advantage, while prediction markets price his re-election at roughly 95 percent. With no polling available, the outlook rests on those fundamentals, which point to a comfortable but not mathematically safe Republican win.
model.watch: A strong national midterm swing against the incumbent's party, or an unexpected scandal, could narrow the margin, though no local polling currently signals such a shift.
notes: No expert rater lists this race; treated as safe for the party holding the seat.
No usable general-election polls; forecast rests on fundamentals and expert ratings.

overview:
Idaho's 2nd District sits firmly in Republican territory, with a partisan lean of thirteen points toward the GOP, and Mike Simpson has held the seat for decades. He enters the general election with a large financial advantage, having raised roughly $1.3 million to Ellie Gilbreath's $161,000, and he carries the name recognition and incumbency benefits of long tenure. Prediction markets price his chances at about 95 percent.

No public polls of the race are available, so the outlook rests on district fundamentals, the money gap, and market pricing. A national environment tilted against the incumbent's party could trim Simpson's margin relative to past cycles, and independent and Libertarian candidates appear on the ballot, but neither factor plausibly threatens his hold. Gilbreath would need a dramatic, unpriced shift to compete; everything measurable points to a comfortable Simpson re-election.
